name: Nested GB: Game Boy -> SNES (proof of concept)
description: Static recompilation of every SM83 instruction the front end finds into 65816 code (HiROM, FastROM): GB registers in direct page, the GB address space in WRAM bank $7F (data bank = GB address), exact GB flags only where a later instruction can read them, a dispatcher with per-address tables for ret / jp (hl) / RAM calls and a small SM83 interpreter (same templates) for self-modifying RAM code. RAM code copied from ROM is translated at its RAM address (feedback: BrokenNes's GB core, Workshop --gbrun --pcs). Picture: GB tiles are SNES 2bpp as they are; dirty 128-byte VRAM chunks are DMA'd in NMI, BGP -> CGRAM, SCX/SCY -> BG1 scroll. Harness: tools/nested-everything/gbpoc_test.py snes.
status: proof of concept: blargg cpu_instrs 06-ld r,r and 01-special pass on BrokenNes's SNES core; 02-interrupts passes #1-#3, fails #4 (no GB timer); no sprites, window, sound, MBC banks beyond 1
